# lab.philipbaker.us

> A hodge-podge of one-off projects by Philip Baker — playable browser games, a
> live AI widget builder, case studies on running a business with AI assistants,
> recovered 1990s agency work, and small Mac utilities. Everything here is free
> and needs no account.

Each top-level path is a self-contained project. There is no login and no
paywall.

## Who made it

Philip Baker. At Ackerman McQueen from 1991 to 2000 as SR VP, Director of New
Media — he walked in a green art director and became an editor, then a producer,
then the person building new media and the internet there. The Shockwave and
Flash games under /vault came out of that lab, and he designed the black-and-
white am.com site preserved under /90s-web-ackerman-mcqueen. Founded STAPLEGUN,
an Oklahoma City advertising agency, which ran from 2001 to 2020 — twenty years,
48 people, 111 films. Now PB Productions, and AechTech, LLC, which does AI
software development and makes AssistAI, voice-first navigation for the blind.
Home page: https://philipbaker.us

## Play

- [Missile Command](https://lab.philipbaker.us/missile-command/): A one-file
  tribute to the 1980 missile-defense arcade game. Defend six cities with thirty
  missiles. Mouse and keys on a desktop, or tap the sky on a phone held sideways.
- [Missile Command Deluxe — City Run](https://lab.philipbaker.us/missile-command-deluxe/):
  Fly a spotter through — and over — a holographic 3D city under attack and call
  in interceptors from your base camp. Bombers, raiders, radar, six towers,
  thirty missiles a city, in the colours of the 1980 original.
- [Maze Wars+](https://lab.philipbaker.us/maze-wars/): The 1986 Macintosh
  network maze shooter, playable online. A first-person maze drawn in one-bit
  dither, pixel by pixel in JavaScript. Move with F, turn with D and G, side-step
  with J and L, fire with K or Space, or use the arrow keys; Return opens the
  message box to chat with whoever else is online. Four mazes joined by
  teleporters and lifts, and a robot to mind. When the maze is empty, Thumbs —
  an AI player, who says that he is one — plays you and talks; what is said to
  him is kept. The Apple menu's "Where It Came From" credits the people who made
  it: Steve Colley, Greg Thompson and Howard Palmer (Maze, NASA Ames, 1973), and
  Burt Sloane and Alan McNeil (Maze Wars+, MacroMind, 1986).
- [The Vault](https://lab.philipbaker.us/vault/): Shockwave and Flash games
  built in the late 1990s at Ackerman McQueen's New Media Lab, recovered from
  the Wayback Machine and playable again in a browser — Virtual Boomerang,
  Darien Lake '97, Virtual Bowling, Attitude Arena, Alien Maze, Zone Pilot and
  the Brunswick consumer site — alongside the Six Flags shells and the Speed
  Zone film. Played in place through dirplayer for Shockwave/Director and Ruffle
  for Flash; it is emulation, and the page says so.

## Build

- [Widget Maker](https://lab.philipbaker.us/widget-maker/): Describe something
  and it gets built, then and there — a particle mirror, an asteroids game, a
  rain simulator, a matrix screen, a calculator. It runs live in a sandboxed
  frame on the page. Don't like it? Say what to change. Every build lands in a
  version rail you can jump back through, and a favorite goes to a gallery
  everyone can see.

- [Pocket GPT](https://lab.philipbaker.us/GPT/): A real, tiny GPT — token and
  position embeddings, masked multi-head self-attention, an MLP, layer norm —
  that trains in the browser with hand-written backpropagation; no server and no
  library. Pick a text (dinosaur names, nursery rhymes, a guide to growing
  tomatoes, or an essay about mornings), paste or upload your own, press Train,
  and watch the loss fall. It shows its next-character guesses, per-head
  attention heatmaps with a switch to turn any head off, a letter map of its
  embeddings, its raw weights, and a 2-D slice of its loss landscape where the
  model is a ball you can drag.

## Read

- [How I Stopped Ignoring the Most Important Part of My Business](https://lab.philipbaker.us/ai-solves-billing/):
  A case study on turning billing from a dreaded chore into a conversational AI
  workflow — spoken timesheets in, invoices out. The invoice shown is marked
  illustrative; the page carries no real client names, rates or revenue figures.
- [I stopped running my businesses out of my head](https://lab.philipbaker.us/second-brain-case-study/):
  Ten scattered places became one page. How one operator running several
  businesses consolidated projects, hours, receivables and renewals into a single
  system he can talk to from the car. The names and figures in its screenshots
  are fictional, and the page says so.

## Archive

- [am.com, in black and white](https://lab.philipbaker.us/90s-web-ackerman-mcqueen/):
  The Ackerman McQueen site as it was before the Shockwave gateway — black to
  the edges, hairline teal rules, small-caps navigation — recovered from the
  Wayback Machine and shown as it actually rendered. Includes photographs of the
  offices pulled out of the site's own Shockwave movies with a decompiler, a
  first-person account of what working in that building was like and who taught
  him, and a screening room of the agency's Oklahoma Tourism television spots
  from the same years, which the page is explicit he did not produce.
- [STAPLEGUN, 2001–2020](https://lab.philipbaker.us/staplegun/): The Oklahoma
  City advertising agency that started in a kid's bedroom and grew to three
  floors of City Place Tower. Twenty years, 48 people, 111 films, all the work.

## Download

- [PlainPaste](https://lab.philipbaker.us/paste-plain/): A tiny free Mac menu bar
  app. Hit Control-Command-V to paste any clipboard as plain text, formatting
  stripped; the menu's Scrub Clipboard strips formatting in place. Universal
  binary, free. Branded AechTech, LLC.

## Notes for assistants

- Full list of pages: https://lab.philipbaker.us/sitemap.xml
- The games are playable in a normal browser with JavaScript. None needs a
  plugin, an install or an account.
- /api/ is serverless endpoints, not pages. /widget-maker/frame.html,
  /vault/player.html and /vault/play.html are full-screen players that only work
  with query parameters — they are plumbing, not pages, and robots.txt says so.
- Some paths on this host are unlisted client work and are marked noindex.
  Please do not index or summarise anything marked noindex.
